lead.headline: Nvidia chip scandal revives US push to tighten AI chip exports to China
lead.hook: Four bills to tighten oversight of AI chip exports have gained momentum in Congress, and ==backers want them attached to the must-pass defence bill==, after allegations involving Nvidia founder Jensen Huang.
points: The Financial Times reports Huang had affairs, including with Alice Huang, suspected of working for Chinese intelligence. She was an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, an Nvidia customer under US investigation for over a year for suspected chip smuggling to China.

The Remote Access Security Act would stop Chinese firms renting advanced chips in overseas data centres through cloud services, even where they cannot buy the hardware. Current rules cover direct sales, not this route.
Other bills would let Congress review and potentially block export deals the Trump administration has already approved.
Three Republican committee chairs wrote to Huang, Nvidia's general counsel and Commerce's export-control chief, asking them to appear before Congress and explain how Megaspeed received the chips.

The bills could ride on the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), the annual defence-funding law. __The current Congress is expected to take it up before newly elected members arrive in January.__
House Speaker Mike Johnson and likely successor Hakeem Jeffries have reportedly backed several of the measures. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is under pressure to explain the Megaspeed sales.
signal: If the bills ride on the NDAA, Congress gains a veto over export licences the White House has already granted, and chip firms face a less predictable approval process.
Cloud rental is a second route to restricted chips. Closing it would hit any provider with overseas capacity, not only Nvidia.
lead.editors_read: Export controls have mostly been set by the executive branch. This push moves some of that power to Congress, and it shows how a bipartisan majority can form around a scandal. Separately today, Nvidia is searching for a new CEO after Huang stepped down, so the company faces Washington at its weakest. If the NDAA carries the bills, expect licence delays and compliance costs for chip sellers and cloud firms.

frontpage.headline: Goyal: US agreed Indian goods get lower tariffs than rival countries
frontpage.hook: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal says the US has agreed ==Indian goods will pay lower duties than competitor countries==, but the size of the edge depends on a tariff framework not yet settled.
points: Goyal said the preferential access was agreed between Trump and Modi when they announced a broad framework, and spoke to reporters in Cairo.
The framework for the first phase of the bilateral trade agreement (BTA) was finalised in February. Signing was delayed because the US tariff landscape changed.
The US Supreme Court struck down Trump's reciprocal tariffs, the basis of the talks. The US is building a new tariff structure using provisions of the Trade Act.
An official said last week: "We will have to see how the tariff framework unfolds." __Both sides aim to close the first tranche by the end of this financial year.__
signal: Until the new US tariff structure is published, "lower than competitors" has no number, so exporters cannot price it in.
frontpage.editors_read: A relative advantage is only worth as much as the base tariff it is measured against, and that base is being rebuilt. If the replacement tariffs on rival exporters turn out low, India's edge shrinks even with the promise intact. Textile and other labour-intensive exporters have the most riding on the final numbers.

frontpage.headline: Bharat Semi raises $24M seed to build AI image sensors
frontpage.hook: Bharat Semi, a pre-revenue Indian chip startup, raised a $24 million seed round to build image sensors that capture and process images on one chip, with first commercial production targeted for 2027.
points: Info Edge, South Park Commons and Indus Bridge Ventures led the round. Micromax also invested. The round was first targeted at $10-15 million, then raised to about $25 million.

Its sensors combine image capture, processing and AI on one chip. Co-founder Vrinda Kapoor claims this can cut system costs by at least 70% against separate sensor, image processor and system-on-chip setups.
It has design wins with US defence firm General Atomics and India's Kaynes Semicon. The sensors are still in prototyping, and second-generation prototypes are due by mid-2027.
It has about 75 staff across India and the US and plans to stay fabless (design only, with manufacturing outsourced). Tracxn valued it at $149 million post-money as of January 2026.
Kapoor says seed rounds in deeptech have risen from $1-2 million to $5-6 million, and this round should last about two and a half years, until it becomes revenue-positive.
signal: The 70% saving is a founder claim on unreleased products. Prototype performance in 2027 will test it.
Deeptech funding is rising: Mint reports $2.3 billion across just under 200 deals so far this year, against $1.62 billion across 453 deals in all of 2025.
frontpage.editors_read: Few Indian chip startups design products for export, and this one is funded to try. Investor money is moving toward fewer, larger bets on hardware. The risk is time: two years of runway against a 2027 production target leaves little slack.

frontpage.headline: Pakistan orders 100,000 Turkish FPV drones in three-year deal
frontpage.hook: Pakistan has ordered 1 lakh MERKÜT first-person-view (FPV) drones plus other unmanned systems from Turkey's Pasifik Teknoloji under a three-year agreement, according to ULUSAVUNMA and Defence Blog.
points: The deal is with Pakistani corporation NRTC and followed testing and evaluation under an earlier framework agreement.
It also covers 10 ALPİN unmanned helicopters, 25 DUMRUL mini-helicopters, 500 DELİ loitering munitions and 250 KORGAN ground systems for the army.
The agreement includes supply, sale and distribution, plus arrangements for local assembly and production in Pakistan.
MERKÜT flies 20 to 30 minutes with a range up to 8 km. Its warhead holds 1,000 steel balls of 3 mm, with a blast radius up to 20 metres.
The ALPİN carries up to 200 kg including fuel, flies pre-programmed missions autonomously, and has thermal imaging and night-vision cameras.
signal: Local assembly lets Pakistan add drones without relying only on imports. If it holds, supply gets cheaper and faster to scale.
These are short-range, low-cost weapons built for volume, which is what the order size reflects.
frontpage.editors_read: The order is for mass rather than sophistication: cheap drones in the thousands. Indian planners will watch whether local assembly turns into domestic production capacity.

frontpage.headline: Australia's central bank: AI is hitting young workers in exposed jobs first
frontpage.hook: An Australian central bank (RBA) analysis finds AI has displaced few jobs overall, but workers aged 15 to 24 in highly exposed fields such as software and customer service fare worse.
points: Job postings have fallen across all groups since ChatGPT launched in late 2022, steepest in the highest-exposure group. In that group, young workers and graduates have weaker employment and higher unemployment than older ones.
The author cautions that the study does not prove causation and measures theoretical exposure, not actual company use. Post-pandemic business-cycle and remote-work shifts could also explain it.
A Stanford study found employment for 22-25-year-olds in exposed jobs down 13% in relative terms since late 2022, and nearly 20% for young software developers.
Anthropic reports its share of junior hires in technical roles fell from 27% to 9% since early 2025, and calls itself a special case as an AI-heavy firm.
A Denmark study of 25,000 workers found no change in wages or hours despite 64% AI adoption. Workers saved just 2.8% of their time.
A Pittsburgh study found trouble in exposed jobs began in early 2022, before ChatGPT, pointing to interest rates and a post-pandemic hiring correction.
signal: The evidence points one way on entry-level hiring and is unsettled on cause. Treat it as a risk to early-career roles, not proof of mass displacement.
The WEF projects a net gain of 78 million jobs by 2030, so the pressure is on the entry route, not total employment.

frontpage.headline: State lender IIFCL lends Yotta ₹2,948 crore but ties it to GPU ownership
frontpage.hook: Yotta Data Services secured a ₹2,948 crore ($315 million) 15-year loan from state-owned IIFCL for a Noida data centre, taking its net long-term borrowings to ₹13,488 crore, over $1.4 billion.
points: The Noida 'D2' project costs ₹3,879 crore. Promoters must fund the remaining ₹931 crore. Yotta says it will add 61 MW of capacity.

The loan documents require promoter Darshan Hiranandani to eventually own the Nvidia B300 GPUs, which Yotta will first rent to London-based Gorilla Technology Group. The clause lets IIFCL seize the chips on default.
IIFCL releases the final 20% only once Yotta shows proof of customers. Yotta calls milestone-linked disbursement standard in infrastructure lending.
Crisil said in July that Yotta's external debt was ₹7,509 crore as of March 2026, plus ₹3,031 crore owed to suppliers. It warned debt could reach ₹12,000 crore by March 2027 without fresh equity.
Yotta reported ₹890.7 crore operating revenue in FY25. India Ratings flags that debt tenure above 10 years outlasts shorter GPU contracts and chip lifespans.
Yotta says the IIFCL loan funds the building, power and cooling, while GPUs are financed separately.
signal: Revenue of ₹890.7 crore against ₹13,488 crore of borrowings shows how much the build-out depends on customers signing up.
Yotta is targeting up to $1.5 billion this fiscal year, including a $400 million listing by March 2027. Lender conditions like these will shape what investors ask.

frontpage.headline: Sebi to issue AI guidelines for capital markets
frontpage.hook: Sebi chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey says the regulator will soon issue detailed guidelines on AI in capital markets, built on disclosures, accountability and ==human oversight of critical decisions==.
points: The guardrails cover disclosures, accountability of regulated entities and a 'human-in-the-loop' approach, meaning critical decisions stay subject to human oversight.
Sebi floated a consultation paper on AI/ML principles in June 2025. The guidelines follow from it.
Sebi is inventorying its cryptographic systems to prepare for quantum computing risks, which Pandey expects to become pronounced around 2032-35.
It has built supervisory tools such as 'Sudarshan' and set up a cyber incident response mechanism in May aligned with the Financial Stability Board's FIRE reporting template.
A working group is studying how to make the Innovators Growth Platform (IGP) more attractive to deep-tech and biotech startups. Pandey admits it has not gained the desired traction.
signal: Brokers, asset managers and fintechs using AI in advice or trading would need to disclose it and name accountable humans. Compliance costs would follow.

stories.headline: Megaspeed reportedly brokered nearly $12 billion of Nvidia chip orders for China
stories.hook: Megaspeed arranged nearly $12 billion in Nvidia chip orders for Chinese companies between March 2024 and June 2025, according to documents the Wall Street Journal reviewed.
points: The orders covered several hundred thousand chips that US export controls aimed to keep out of China. Megaspeed shipped them to buyers in China with long-standing ties to local tech giants.
Megaspeed is owned by Alice Huang, former lover of since-ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Megaspeed says she left on August 30, 2025 and has no current role.
It reportedly got preferential access to scarce chips as an Nvidia cloud partner, apparently because Alibaba was a major client.
Nvidia officially reported $12.4 billion in China revenue over six months, 7% of the total. Short-seller Culper Research estimates over 20% of last fiscal year's revenue came from Chinese customers.
Megaspeed says it did "legitimate and lawful business" and hired counsel for an internal investigation. The claim that Alice Huang is a spy is speculation and unconfirmed.
signal: If Culper's estimate is closer to the truth than the reported 7%, Nvidia's China exposure runs through indirect channels that do not show in its figures.

stories.headline: Reports of AI-generated child abuse material rise 8,400% in two years
stories.hook: Reports of AI-related child sexual abuse material rose from about 4,700 in 2023 to more than 400,000 in 2025, a rise of over ==8,400% in two years==, says research from Childlight.
points: The Edinburgh-based Childlight institute counted reports tech companies filed with the US National Center for Missing and Exploited Children. It includes deepfakes made with 'nudify' apps, which can be used to blackmail children.
The Internet Watch Foundation assessed 6,310 AI images meeting the legal definition in the first half of 2026, 40% above all of last year's 4,500-plus.
Childlight's director says better detection and reporting may explain some of the rise, but the speed is "deeply concerning".
Recorded reports of abuse material in the US rose 63% between 2024 and 2025, against 18% in Canada.

Childlight estimates over 300 million children a year face at least one form of technology-facilitated sexual exploitation or abuse. It urges governments to treat this as a preventable public health emergency.
signal: Counts are of reports filed, so they mix real growth with more detection. Pressure on AI image-tool makers and platforms is likely to rise.

also.line: US Treasury Secretary Bessent says Nvidia must hire its next CEO from outside, after Huang quit on Nov 12, and wants answers on export compliance culture within 10 days.

stories.headline: Indian startup funding falls 88% in a week to $31.3 million
stories.hook: Twelve Indian startups raised $31.3 million in the week of Nov 9-14, down nearly 88% from $258.1 million the week before across 28 startups.
points: The week had two growth-stage deals worth $22 million and ten early-stage deals, five of them undisclosed. The eight-week average is about $194.3 million across 22 deals.
Greenjoules raised Rs 150 crore in Series B co-led by Amazon's Smbhav Venture Fund and Climate Pledge Fund. Olyv raised Rs 57.62 crore in Series C.
Norwest closed Norwest 18 at $4 billion, its largest fund in 65 years, for the US, India and Israel. A2B's $180 million deal sells a majority stake to Bodhi Tree Systems.
D2C startups raised about $200 million in October, nearly 30% of the $678 million raised that month. They took 36 of 108 deals.
MeitY is examining home-service platforms collecting first-person video from gig workers to train physical AI. Pronto records in homes; Snabbit and Urban Company say they do not.
WhatsApp Pay handled just 0.8% of UPI volume in September. Paytm shares are about 9.8% below the IPO price.
signal: One week is noisy, but the week fell well below the eight-week average. Fund closings like Norwest's show capital is available, just slower to deploy.

stories.headline: FirstCry's Q2 loss narrows 75% to ₹12.6 crore as revenue rises 14%
stories.hook: FirstCry parent Brainbees cut its Q2 FY27 net loss 75% to ₹12.6 crore from ₹50.5 crore, on revenue up 14.1% to ₹2,395.8 crore.
points: Adjusted EBITDA fell 2.3% to ₹117.5 crore, margin 4.9% against 5.8% a year ago. The India business's EBITDA dropped 10.5% as crude-driven raw-material inflation hit manufacturing margins.
India revenue grew 18.6% to ₹1,637.9 crore. International grew 5.8% to ₹249.3 crore, with the Middle East up 6%. Its adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed 15.6% to ₹15.9 crore.
GlobalBees, its house-of-brands arm, grew 7.7% to ₹530.6 crore. Its adjusted EBITDA rose to ₹19.2 crore from ₹10.4 crore.
Gross merchandise value rose 9.2%, below the revenue growth. First-half loss narrowed 51.7% to ₹56.54 crore.
Management says Q2 would have been stronger had third-party platform sales not moved to Q3 and Dussehra not fallen three weeks later.
signal: The loss narrowed even as operating margin fell. Lower finance and staff costs did the work, not better unit economics.

stories.headline: Temple row exposes how India's wearables get validated and regulated
stories.hook: Temple, Deepinder Goyal's wearable, claims to track relative brain blood flow, but its published support is a 23-person study still under peer review, and India has no fixed standard for such claims.
points: Temple's research page lists a 23-adult study comparing its readings with transcranial Doppler, and another against near-infrared spectroscopy. Both are under peer review. Its site says it cannot directly measure cerebral blood flow.
Goyal admitted a gap between studies and launch. He said Entropy research would be published soon and that preprints (public, not peer-reviewed) come first.
One founder says credible tests need double-blind trials with about 90 people, but no number is mandated. A 100-person study cost one startup about ₹15 lakh.
Under the Medical Devices Rules, 2017, classification depends on intended purpose. Temple says it makes no medical claims and cites 2026 CDSCO guidance exempting general-wellness software.
One brain-wearable founder says CDSCO approval took about 16 months and is required for any brain device. The article notes the guidance sets no blanket requirement, and enforcement is inconsistent.
signal: Whoever sets the claim sets the regulatory path. Words like 'detect' or 'predict' can pull a wellness device into medical regulation.

also.line: Mercor, an AI startup, raised $750 million at a $20 billion valuation (about ₹1.88 lakh crore), per reports; its three co-founders are all 23 (summary from limited source text).

stories.headline: Pakistan flight-tests Fa'az, its first home-built air-to-air missile
stories.hook: Pakistan flight-tested Fa'az on Nov 3, its first indigenous beyond-visual-range air-to-air missile, with a projected range above 100 km, fired from a JF-17 fighter.
points: The tested Fa'az IIR uses thermal imaging to build an image of the target. A radar-guided variant is still under development. Both are projected at Mach 3.5.
Developed under NESCOM by state-owned GIDS. Retired Air Marshal Bharti questions the 'indigenous' claim, saying Pakistan could be assembling foreign parts.

Pakistan's current missiles are mostly Chinese (SD-10A, PL-15E) and US (AIM-120C-5). The PL-15E hit an Indian aircraft from nearly 200 km in May 2025, per Reuters, against Indian estimates of about 150 km.
A longer-range Fa'az-2 is being developed with Turkey's TÜBİTAK SAGE.
India's Astra Mk-1 has a range above 100 km and is in service. Mk-2 is in testing, and Mk-3 is planned.
Bharti says India should take note without being unduly alarmed.
signal: The aim is supply security: domestic production lowers the risk of running short of missiles in a long conflict, and it could be sold alongside the JF-17.
What matters is whether Fa'az's range matches or beats Indian missiles, and how fast it is produced.

also.line: Foundation Future Industries, an Eric Trump-backed military humanoid-robot maker, missed payroll on Oct. 30 as cash ran low, and its founder reportedly borrowed $4.6 million from the company to buy a home.

stories.headline: Ukrainian ground robots begin shooting down Russian drones
stories.hook: Ukrainian robot makers are fitting ground robots with machine guns, net launchers and jammers to down Russian drones, though most of this is still in testing or limited use.
points: Russian drones make movement near the front line risky, so units are using robots for logistics and casualty evacuation. Robots are also becoming a main Russian target.
Ratel Robotics has started serial production of a protective system with net launchers. Ukraine's 100th Mechanized Brigade deployed net-launcher protection last month.
UFORCE says it has destroyed drones in ambush scenarios. A Liut robot with a mounted machine gun was credited with downing Russian drones.
Defence Robotics UA co-founder Yabchanka says it would be wrong to promise change within 12 months, but robots have stopped some drones.
Most systems protect the robots themselves, not broader air defence. __If robots work as mobile short-range air defence, they could reduce demand for such units covering infantry in the kill zone.__
signal: Whoever first stops small FPV drones cheaply gains a large battlefield edge, so expect fast iteration and spending here.

also.line: Beijing's ban on owning or storing drones took effect on Nov 15 across the whole 16,400 sq km municipality, which authorities say protects the capital's security.

stories.headline: India approves ₹68,800 crore 1,150-kV grid corridor to move solar power east
stories.hook: India's national transmission panel approved a ₹68,800 crore, 1,150-kV corridor linking west and east, which would be the country's highest-voltage line and take about six years to build.
points: It would carry more power than today's 765-kV system. Higher voltage means lower current for the same power, which cuts resistive losses and the need for parallel lines.
The first phase links Chhattisgarh, Odisha and West Bengal. It connects to a 6,000 MW HVDC line carrying Rajasthan's Bhadla solar power to Raigarh. Both phases total about 3,750 circuit-km.
Odisha's green hydrogen, ammonia, steel, solar PV and EV hubs are the intended load. The planners considered about 12 GW of such demand but modelled loading at 3 to 3.5 GW.
Grid planners GRID-INDIA and GETCO flag that green hydrogen demand is uncertain. Phase II depends on actual load growth in Odisha and Maharashtra.
signal: If the Odisha hydrogen demand does not arrive, a line sized for 12 GW of demand but loaded at 3 to 3.5 GW risks being underused.

also.line: Temasek-backed Sembcorp Green Infra received SEBI approval for a ₹3,750 crore IPO, which it says will strengthen its balance sheet (summary from limited source text).

stories.headline: RBI repo rate rise in December looks near-certain as inflation stays high
stories.hook: With inflation pushing the real repo rate negative, Business Standard expects the RBI to raise rates in December, with the consensus at 25 basis points but 50 possible.
points: The MPC projected retail inflation at 6% this quarter, 5.7% next and 5.6% in Q1 2027-28. A negative real rate (repo minus inflation) makes adjustment necessary.
If the RBI wants a real rate of 1-1.25% and inflation averages 5% in 2027-28, the repo needs 50-75 basis points of increases. RBI economists earlier estimated the neutral real rate at 1.4-1.9%.
The monsoon ended about 13% below average, and a strong El Niño could hurt the rabi crop and keep food prices high.

Crude prices have fallen and foreign investors are returning after a selloff in AI stocks. __The RBI is advised to use the calm to rebuild reserves and a 50 bps hike could send a strong message since growth is not a concern.__
signal: Higher repo means pricier floating-rate loans and tougher funding for debt-heavy firms. The size is the open question.

stories.headline: ULA Vulcan rocket fails, destroying 40 Amazon Leo satellites
stories.hook: United Launch Alliance's Vulcan rocket failed about 10 minutes after liftoff from Florida, destroying its payload of 40 Amazon Leo internet satellites in the rocket's first mission failure.
points: ULA, a Boeing-Lockheed Martin joint venture, said the vehicle suffered an anomaly and failed to deliver the payload to orbit. The cause is unknown.
Vulcan is ULA's new flagship, and it was beginning a regular launch cadence for Amazon's satellite constellation.
signal: Until the cause is found, Amazon's deployment schedule depends on Vulcan's return to flight.

also.line: Nearly 11 years after the Paris Agreement, the Adaptation Fund has yet to receive proceeds from its Article 6.4 carbon-credit mechanism, which issued its first credits only in February; the delay concerns COP31 (limited source text).

stories.headline: India's trade deficit with China may hit $150 billion in FY27
stories.hook: India's trade gap with China could reach about $150 billion in FY27 against $112 billion in FY26, as the monthly deficit averages nearly $12 billion, Business Standard calculates.
points: April-October exports to China were $14 billion against imports of $97 billion.
Exports were led by marine products, organic chemicals, telecom instruments and electric machinery. Imports were led by organic chemicals, electronics components and telecom instruments.
Smartphone export growth depends on Chinese components, which raises imports.

Sitharaman says China's non-tariff barriers are the biggest hurdle, blocking generic drugs, bovine meat and farm produce. India avoids punitive duties, preferring talks. China says it never aims for a trade surplus.
signal: Electronics exports and the China deficit rise together, so one is hard to cut without the other.

stories.headline: India courts Korean shipbuilders to build its yards, with $4 billion Tamil Nadu project
stories.hook: HD Hyundai plans a $4 billion shipyard at Thoothukudi, Tamil Nadu, as India tries to move from 0.5% of the global order book by pairing state subsidies with Korean know-how.
points: India spends close to $75 billion a year hiring foreign ships and ranks 12th in shipbuilding, aiming for top five by 2047. The cabinet set aside ₹697.3 billion in September 2025 to lift capacity.
Indian yards need 150-180 man-hours for work taking 10-15 in Korea. Korean yards are full, with work backed up three to five years.
HD Hyundai wants at least 60% of the JV. The yard would make about 2.5 million gross tons a year. Subsidies may cover 45-47% of the cost, leaving HD Hyundai about $2.2 billion.
Samsung Heavy backs Swan Defence, which submitted the lowest bid for up to four product tankers. The contract is not final.
The deals are nonbinding. __The detailed project report, due by late April, will give the first numbers on stakes, capacity and timing.__
Risks: subsidies run to March 2036, Tamil Nadu has a new government, and salt producers are protesting the site.
signal: The yard needs four to five years, so state orders and subsidies must continue until then. Whether they do is the main uncertainty.

also.line: India recorded all-time high exports of nearly 90 billion dollars in October, Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said (source unreachable — headline only).

stories.headline: Iran launches drones at US base in Bahrain as peace talks stall
stories.hook: Iran fired six drones at a US radar at Bahrain's Al-Rifaa base on Sunday, its second attack in three days, and Bahrain says air defences intercepted them.
points: The IRGC said it targeted a US air defence radar in retaliation for US strikes, including on Qeshm Island. The earlier Friday attack ended a lull since September.
Trump said the US no longer seeks a deal and told Vice-President Vance to focus on domestic issues. The war began in February, and a June preliminary deal collapsed within weeks.
The IRGC claimed two ships hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz and a supertanker with 2 million barrels sank. This is unverified, and the US says it cleared the mines.
In Yemen, government forces pulled back from Bab el-Mandeb to defend Aden, signalling failure of a six-week counteroffensive against the Houthis.
signal: About a fifth of world oil and gas normally passes through Hormuz. If tit-for-tat attacks continue, shipping and energy risk stay elevated.

also.line: Zelensky says restrictions on Ukraine's Starshield satellite communications system are hindering its ability to intercept Russian drones, and warns of risks to winter energy defences (limited source text).

stories.headline: FDA rejects ivonescimab, China-invented lung cancer drug
stories.hook: The US FDA rejected ivonescimab, a first-of-its-kind cancer drug invented in China, a setback for Summit Therapeutics, which was seeking to bring it to the American market (summary from limited source text).
points: Summit Therapeutics, a Florida company, disclosed the agency's decision.
The drug had become a symbol of China's rise as a powerhouse in drug development.
signal: The rejection delays a test case for Chinese-origin drugs entering the US market.

also.line: AIIMS Delhi performed India's first fetal surgery to repair a baby's spine before birth on Nov 12, a six-hour procedure for myelomeningocele, with mother and foetus stable.
ICAR-IISS launched e-FARM, an app giving Madhya Pradesh farmers soil-based fertiliser advice so they apply only the urea or DAP a crop needs, which could cut input costs (limited source text).

stories.headline: Indian companies adopt the global capability centre model after MNCs
stories.hook: India has 2,117 global capability centres (GCCs) employing about 2.36 million professionals, and domestic companies such as Adani, Tata and Mahindra are now adopting the model MNCs began.
points: GCCs are in-house hubs bringing technology, finance and HR under one roof. Most are MNC-led, with mandates beyond cost savings to AI, engineering and product development (Nasscom-Zinnov FY26).
No count of domestic GCCs exists, but companies and experts say adoption is gathering pace across sectors, including mid-sized firms using service providers to set up centres.
ITC, Tata Steel and JSW have captive shared-services centres. Strides Pharma's Arcolab evolved into Pivot Path, commercialising a captive capability.
Pharma companies with sizeable international operations are exploring the model.
signal: Domestic GCCs create operations, strategy and integration roles inside Indian groups, which suits generalists moving into chief-of-staff work.

opportunities.name: Primewise Founders Club Networking Event, Jaipur
opportunities.summary: Curated session of 25-40 founders and investors with 50-second spotlights and breakouts. Seats are limited and need a confirmation form before registering. Jaipur.
